subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the overall shape of a DNA molecule?
questions.explain: DNA is made of two strands twisted together into a shape called a double helix.

questions.q: DNA is a polymer made of repeating units called:
questions.explain: The building blocks (monomers) of DNA are nucleotides, each containing a sugar, a phosphate and a base.

questions.q: Which four bases are found in DNA?
questions.explain: DNA contains the four bases adenine, thymine, cytosine and guanine.

questions.q: In DNA, adenine always pairs with:
questions.explain: Adenine always pairs with thymine through complementary base pairing.

questions.q: Which two bases pair together in DNA?
questions.explain: Cytosine always pairs with guanine, just as adenine pairs with thymine.

questions.q: What makes up the two 'uprights' (backbone) of the DNA double helix?
questions.explain: The sides of the DNA ladder are formed from alternating sugar and phosphate groups, with paired bases forming the rungs.

questions.q: One strand of DNA has the base sequence A-T-G-C-A. What is the sequence of the complementary strand?
questions.explain: Using complementary base pairing (A-T and C-G), A-T-G-C-A pairs with T-A-C-G-T.

questions.q: Base pairing in DNA is described as 'complementary' because:
options: Each base pairs with only one other specific base
All four bases can pair with each other
Each base pairs with a sugar group
questions.explain: Complementary means each base can only join with one specific partner: A with T and C with G.

questions.q: What is a gene?
options: A section of DNA that codes for a protein
questions.explain: A gene is a section of DNA that carries the code for making a particular protein.

questions.q: How many chromosomes are found in a normal human body cell?
questions.explain: A human body cell contains 46 chromosomes, arranged as 23 pairs.

questions.q: The 46 chromosomes in a human body cell are arranged as:
questions.explain: The 46 chromosomes are found as 23 matching pairs, one of each pair from each parent.

questions.q: Chromosomes are made of:
questions.explain: Each chromosome is a long molecule of DNA coiled up tightly.

questions.q: Which statement about genes and chromosomes is correct?
options: A single chromosome carries many genes
Each chromosome carries exactly one gene
Genes are found only outside the nucleus
questions.explain: A chromosome is a long strand of DNA that contains many genes.

questions.q: A human body cell contains 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes were inherited from each parent?
questions.explain: Each parent contributes one chromosome of every pair, so 23 chromosomes come from each parent.

questions.q: What determines the order of amino acids in a protein?
options: The order of bases in the gene
The total amount of DNA in the cell
questions.explain: The sequence of bases in a gene determines the sequence of amino acids that make up the protein.

questions.q: How many bases in the DNA code for one amino acid?
questions.explain: A sequence of three bases codes for one amino acid.

questions.q: In a cell, proteins are assembled at the:
questions.explain: Proteins are built by joining amino acids together at the ribosomes.

questions.q: What is the role of mRNA in protein synthesis?
options: It carries a copy of the genetic code from the nucleus to the ribosome
It permanently stores the DNA in the nucleus
It joins amino acids together into fats
questions.explain: mRNA carries a copy of the gene's code out of the nucleus to the ribosome, where the protein is made.

questions.q: A protein is made of a chain of 4 amino acids. What is the minimum number of DNA bases needed to code for it?
questions.explain: As three bases code for one amino acid, 4 amino acids need 4 x 3 = 12 bases.

questions.q: Where in the cell are chromosomes found?
questions.explain: Chromosomes are located inside the nucleus of the cell.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Biology (2017) specification; Chromosomes, Genes & DNA
